courseContributions.ACCPPDE101: Mandatory Year-1 personal/professional and academic development.
courseContributions.GOSGATE102: Case law, trial simulations and legal/social/normative perspectives establish the integrated law-and-society foundation.
courseContributions.GOSLAWJ111: Human-rights treaties, monitoring/case law and natural-law philosophy connect legal protection to justice and ethical argument.
courseContributions.GOSSOCI111: Sociological theories and institutions, race/gender and colonial contexts provide a social explanation of the settings in which law operates.
courseContributions.BENGATE102: Research design, sampling, operationalisation, inference/ANOVA and a group project supply empirical methods for investigating law-related social questions.
courseContributions.HCBPSYC111: Social influences on judgments, attitudes and behaviour supply the psychological perspective needed to interpret legal actors and public responses.
courseContributions.GOSSOCI212: Research design, interviews/meaning, data interpretation and reflexivity supply qualitative methods before later applied empirical work.
courseContributions.DISARIN111: Fairness, bias, privacy, responsibility and AI decision-making provide ethical/psychological analysis relevant to legal AI; not VU’s computational methods or legal-application training.
courseContributions.BENGATE101: Venture ideation, market validation and business planning explain how firms formulate transactions and commercial models later examined in transnational/platform-business law; not legal doctrine.
courseContributions.GOSLAWJ211: Criminal accountability, guilt, legality, punishment and simulated legal advice implement substantive criminal-law reasoning; criminological causation remains limited.
courseContributions.GOSLAWJ311: Comparative property, tort and contract principles and their social pressures supply the private-law strand of the legal response.
courseContributions.ENSSUST111: Climate mechanisms, social effects, justice and mitigation establish the factual background for evaluating legal/governance climate responses; not treaty or corporate climate law.
courseContributions.BENBUSI311: Cross-border contracts, trade, intellectual property, foreign investment and digital commerce provide substantive transnational business-law analysis.
courseContributions.BENLEAD312: BATNA/ZOPA, bargaining structures, trade-offs and negotiation simulations provide dispute-negotiation skills; mediation procedure is not assumed.
courseContributions.GOSLAWJ212: Public international law, force, international criminal/refugee/environmental law and compliance supply global legal-governance analysis; not a dedicated migration-law sequence.
courseContributions.GOSLAWJ213: Comparative constitutional/administrative principles, state power and rights supply public-law reasoning across legal systems.
courseContributions.GOSPOLI311: EU institutions, legislative dossiers and organised-interest research explain the political process through which legal rules and economic policies are formed.
courseContributions.BENECON111: Consumer/firm incentives, market structure and aggregate economic effects explain behaviour of actors regulated in platform/transnational-business settings; not legal protection itself.
courseContributions.GOSPHIL111: Theoretical tools, knowledge, responsibility and rigorous argumentation support reflective legal/normative reasoning; not a dedicated philosophy-of-law course.
courseContributions.HCBPSYC315: Evidence-based youth resilience and participation in an international research project supply a specific prevention/empirical contribution to extremism; not terrorism offences or sanctions law.
courseContributions.GOSPOLI212: Competing international-relations explanations and a SecurityCouncilsimulation supply institutional/political perspectives on global legal governance.
courseContributions.GOSLAWJ312: EU legal institutions, rights, citizenship and free movement analysed through cases/PBL supply the multilevel European-law strand.
courseContributions.GOSPOLI313: Conflict causes, violence, structural inequality and peacebuilding/reconciliation explain social problems addressed by security and justice institutions; not criminal doctrine.
courseContributions.ENSDELT312: Rule-making, governmental/nonstate actors, interests and sustainability policy/enforcement supply governance analysis complementary to environmental law; not professional legal ethics.

rejectedSecondary: Coherent15EClegalanchor is not enough to establish the integrated legal/empirical concept when remainingbusiness/environmental courses do not provide the missing legal mechanisms. Wholeworkbookreconstruction would reuse retainedlawcourses, not yield the proposed distinctbusinessprogramme.
